author: simulation_agent

inequalities.inequality: dt <= recovery_time / steps_per_recovery_min: the step resolves the bleach, the only time-dependent term; free diffusion itself sets no stability limit

numbers.name: recovery_time
numbers.note: tau of the registered fit at the operating point; half recovery is 0.895 tau

numbers.name: steps_per_recovery_min
numbers.note: engine steps per recovery time. The shortest bleach worth planning is a few hundredths of tau, and a few steps across it needs of order a hundred steps per tau

numbers.name: integration_timestep_max
numbers.note: the longest engine step. Not a stability bound: free Brownian increments are exact at any dt

assumptions.statement: The bleach is applied once per engine step, so a bleach a few steps long is a few kicks rather than a continuous exposure. Four steps across the shortest bleach worth running keeps the kick sequence close to continuous; the dt-halving point of the plan measures whether it is.
assumptions.falsifier: a fitted D that moves by more than three standard errors when the step is halved

note: bd_overdamped's tracer A1 bounds dt by curvature and the diffusive time. Neither enters here: there is no potential, and the bead size never appears in a column bleach
